scenario: AITA for being uncomfortable when my boyfriend speaks Spanish to his family around me? | I’m very rarely with my boyfriend and his family, but the few times I have been, they’d only communicate with one another through Spanish, which is a language I hardly know at all. His whole family speaks English as well, but they choose to speak Spanish to one another around me, which makes me uncomfortable because a lot of times it’s regarding plans we’ve made and then my boyfriend has to turn to me and translate what they’ve all been saying, and often he leaves things out and forgets to tell me those necessary details until later. Now of course I don’t mind if it’s like, his siblings to his mother in a conversation that shouldn’t involve me, but when they’re talking with my boyfriend as he’s sitting right next to me, I just feel weird. I understand it’s their “normal language” as my boyfriend calls it, and I’m not trying to be all up in the business or try to have them change their ways, it just makes me feel left out and extremely confused and even a little awkward... I’ve mentioned it to him and he gets defensive and angry, like they’re not going to change to make me more comfortable. I just feel that if the roles were reversed, I would have my family speak to me in a language my boyfriend would understand so he wouldn’t feel left out or like he’s missing something important. Before anyone tells me to simply learn Spanish, first of all, it’s not that easy and second, I am learning Spanish...trying to at least... I feel like I AM the asshole but I don’t want to be...so someone just tell me, am I the asshole?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being unreasonable or not in this situation with my boyfriend and his family. Let me start by laying out what's happening. I don't speak much Spanish, so when they're talking in Spanish, especially about plans we've made, it makes me feel left out and confused. My boyfriend has to translate things for me, but he often leaves out details or forgets to tell me important stuff until later. That's frustrating because I feel like I'm missing out on important information. I understand that Spanish is their normal language, and I don't want to come off as demanding or trying to change their ways. But when they're talking with my boyfriend while he's sitting right next to me, it just feels weird. I feel like if the roles were reversed, I would have my family speak in a language my boyfriend understands so he wouldn't feel left out or confused. I've mentioned this to my boyfriend, but he gets defensive and angry, saying they're not going to change to make me more comfortable. That makes me feel like I'm the asshole, but I don't want to be. Am I being unreasonable? I don't want to be the asshole, but I also don't want to feel excluded and confused all the time. I need to figure out if my feelings are justified or if I'm overreacting. Maybe I should consider why they choose to speak Spanish around me. Is it because they're more comfortable, or is it something else? I don't want to assume the worst, but it's hard not to feel excluded when they're talking in a language I don't understand, especially about things that involve me. I also wonder if there's a way to communicate my feelings without making my boyfriend defensive. But at the same time, I'm part of the family now, and I want to feel included. I also need to reflect on whether I'm making an effort to learn Spanish. I'm trying, but it's taking time, and I feel like I'm not getting anywhere fast. Maybe I need to be more patient with myself and continue learning without feeling pressured. Overall, I'm torn between respecting their language and wanting to feel included and informed. I don't want to come off as entitled, but I also don't want to feel left out all the time. I need to find a balance where both my feelings and their comfort are respected. Perhaps I can set some boundaries or find a compromise. Maybe they can speak English when discussing plans that involve me, or my boyfriend can make a conscious effort to include me in the conversations. It's a delicate situation, and I need to approach it carefully to avoid making things worse. In the end, I want to feel valued and included in our relationship and family dynamics.
